The petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking to award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in the road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
On 17.11.2023 at about 6.50 am., the petitioner was standing on the extreme left side of Devinagara Cross Bus SCCH - 26 3 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 Stop, Bhadrappa Layout,
situated on Ring Road for waiting the bus in order to go to her duty at Manipal Hospital, Yeshwanthapura.

At that time, the rider of KTM Avenger- 250 Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KL-8554 suddenly came from Hebbal towards B.E.L. side in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life,
without observing any of the traffic rules and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein X-rays were taken, which reveals abrasion over the face, mild swelling right maxillary region, left knee swelling present on lateral aspect, severe injuries to hand, legs.
The petitioner was treated with analgesics and dressing was done and discharged.

Due to severe pain, the petitioner once again taken treatment in the aforesaid hospital as an inpatient from 20.11.2023 to 22.11.2023,
MRI was done, which shows left knee lateral condyle depressed fracture, for which she has undergone surgery on 21.11.2023.
The petitioner SCCH - 26 4 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 was discharged with an advise to take follow-up treatment, restricted fracture movements and complete bed rest with suitable exercises.

Petitioner has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance,
nourishment and other incidental charges.

The injuries sustained by the petitioner was not recovered, she is getting unbearable pain,
headache, giddiness, she cannot walk stand, sit, squat on floor, use Indian type of toilet, carry weight, cannot chew hard food.
There are scar marks present over the face, due to which the petitioner looking ugly and she is suffering from pain and the injuries caused to her are permanent in nature.
Further submitted that prior to the accident petitioner was hale and healthy, she was working as a Nurse at Manipal Hospital, Yeshwanthapur, Bengaluru and she was earning Rs.28,000/- p.m.
She was maintained her family members, since she is the only earning member in the family.
Due to accidental injuries, the petitioner cannot attend to her work which resulted the loss of earning, earning capacity and she put to great financial hardship.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the KTM Avenger-250 Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KL-8554 by its rider and in this connection, the Hebbal Traffic Police have registered the case in Cr.No.214/2023 and filed charge sheet punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC against the said rider.

At the time of accident, the first respondent being the R.C owner of the aforesaid KTM Avenger-250 motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 04-KL-8554 and the 2nd respondent being the insurer, the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Accordingly, the petitioner has prayed to award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- together with cost and interest.
6. After service of summons, Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared through their respective counsels and filed objection statements.
7. Respondent No.1-R.C. owner of the offending vehicle has filed objection by denying the entire petition averments.
He has denied the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider, injuries and disability sustained by the petitioner, treatment taken by her and amount spent towards treatment.
Further denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
He has contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and unreasonable without any legal basis.

Further contended that, petitioner was not followed the rules and the accident was took place due to her fault, not for the fault of the driver of 1st respondent, but the said fact was suppressed by the petitioner and filed false case only to grab the money.
Further contended that, in the accident place heavy vehicles are moving and it is the busy road, hence it shows that, due to negligence of the petitioner the accident was happened.
Further contended that, at the time of accident, insurance policy was valid, hence the 2nd respondent is responsible to pay compensation.
For all these, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.

8. Respondent No.2 - Insurer of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KL-8554 has filed objection contending that, SCCH - 26 7 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further contended that, the accident was occurred on 17.11.2923, but it was reported to police on 19.11.2023 i.e., after delay of 2 days and it appears that, the offending motor cycle was falsely implicated to the accident only to get compensation.

This respondent has admitted the Gangamma C vs Deekshith M on 12 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57391937/
3 issuance of insurance policy with respect to offending vehicle and contended that, the liability if any is subject to validity of RC, FC and driving licence of the rider of above said vehicle.

This respondent has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

Further denied the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider, injuries sustained by the petition, treatment taken and amount spent by her towards treatment, age, occupation and income of the petitioner.

It is contended that, the petitioner had to wait for the bus at the bus shelter on the footpath provided for the safety of the commuters, but she had stepped down on the road and thereby she has violated the traffic rules, hence the accident SCCH - 26 8 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 was occurred due to own negligence of the petitioner.
Without proper investigation the police have registered the case against the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04- KL-8554 to help the petitioner only to get compensation.
The owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
The rider of offending vehicle had no valid driving licence to ride the same as on the date of accident, which is clear violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence this respondent is not liable to pay compensation.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

9. On the basis of the above pleadings, following issues have been framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, on 17.11.2023 at about 6.50 a.m., when she was standing on the extreme left side at Devinagara Cross Bus stop, Bhadrappa layout,
Bangalore, at that time, the rider of the KRM Avenger-25- Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KL-8554 came from Hebbal towards B.E.L. SCCH - 26 9 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 side in a rash and negligent manner without observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident, due to the impact, she was fell down sustained grievous injuries mentioned in the petition?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so,
from which respondent?
3. What Order or Award?
10. In order to prove her case, the petitioner herself examined as PW.1 and got marked 30 documents as per Ex.P.1 to 30.
She has examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N., as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.P.31 and Ex.P.32.
The respondents have not adduced the rebuttal evidence, hence respondents evidence is taken as nil.
11. Heard the arguments on both sides.
Perused the entire records.

12. My findings to the above issues are as under:

Issue No.1:

At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

Again it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs. Balaji and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder:
" Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold SCCH - 26 11 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 that, the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to proves the same".

In order to prove the actionable negligence on the part of rider of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KL-8554, petitioner has got examined herself as PW.1.
She has filed affidavit by way of examination in chief and she has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
In order to prove issue No.1, she has produced documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9.

Out of which, Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P.2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the spot panchanama, Ex.P.4 is the hand sketch map, Ex.P.5 is the wound certificate, Ex.P.6 is the MVA report, Ex.P.7 is the final report, Ex.P.8 is the notice issued under Sec.133 of M.V. Act and Ex.P.9 is the reply to the notice U/Sec.133 of M.V. Act.
The oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner proves that, there was an accident in which she has sustained injuries.

15. With regard to negligence, Respondent No.1 and 2 have mainly contended that, in the accident place heavy SCCH - 26 12 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 vehicles are moving, the petitioner had to wait for the bus at the bus shelter on the footpath provided for the safety of the commuters, but she had stepped down on the road and thereby she has violated the traffic rules, hence the accident was occurred due to own negligence of the petitioner and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of offending vehicle for the cause of accident.
In order to substantiate their contention, respondent No.1 and 2 have not produced any oral or documentary evidence.

On perusal of Ex.P.2, complaint it reveals that one Ranganath has lodged the complaint and on the basis of the said complaint, Hebbal Police have registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 against the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KL-8554.

17. All the records indicate the negligence on the part of rider of the offending KTM Avenger-205 motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KL-8554.
Respondents have also failed to prove the allegations of the petitioner with regard to the injury sustained by her in the alleged accident.

By the above materials and evidences it is clear that the Petitioner has sustained injuries in RTA due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the offending KTM Avenger-205 motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KL-8554.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:
The petitioner has produced her Aadhaar Card at Ex.P.10 to consider her age at the time of accident.

As per Ex.P.10, the date of birth of petitioner is mentioned as 24.04.1999, the accident was occurred on 17.11.2023 and hence the age of petitioner was 24 years at SCCH - 26 14 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 the time of accident.

Therefore by considering the evidence on record and doctor opinion, I am of the opinion that, the disability of the petitioner has to be taking into consideration for his physical disability to award compensation.
So, in view of all these circumstances, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following different heads.
19. In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, she was working as a Nurse at Manipal Hospital, Yeshwanthpur, Bengaluru and she was earning a sum of Rs.28,000/- per month.
Per-contra, the respondent No.1 and 2 have denied the income of petitioner.
To prove her contentions, P.W.1 has produced Ex.P.30, the salary slip for the month of September-2023 issued by the Manipal Hospitals, Yeshwanthpur, Bengaluru.

On perusal the said document, it discloses that,
the petitioner was getting gross salary of Rs.24,535/- and after deduction she was getting net salary of Rs.22,007/-.
In order to prove her avocation and income, the petitioner has not examined her employer.
Moreover the petitioner has produced the salary slip for the SCCH - 26 15 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 month of September-2023, whereas the accident was occurred on 17.11.2023.
During the course of cross- examination, P.W.1 has clearly admitted that, the hospital authorities have remitted her salary to the bank account and she was not joining her duty from November.
But she has not produced any bank statement to show that, she was drawing salary of Rs.28,000/- per month.
Except the oral version of PW1, nothing is available on record to consider the avocation and income of the Petitioner as stated by her.
Therefore the petitioner has failed to prove that, she was drawing salary of Rs.28,000/- per month at the time of accident.
Hence this Tribunal is unable to considered the income of the petitioner as Rs.28,000/- per month at the time of accident.
At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision of Yashoda.H and others V/s. Sharath Kumar Achar and another.

20. PW.1 has stated that, on account of injuries sustained by her, she has sustained abrasions over the face, mild swelling over right maxillary region, left knee swelling and severe injuries to hand and legs.

P.W.1 has deposed that, she was treated in the hospital on 17.11.20223 with analgesics,
dressing done and thereafter she was discharged from the hospital on the same day.
There was nobody to look after her as she went to undergo operation.
P.W.1 further deposed that, later on 20.11.2023, she was again admitted to the Manipal hospital, wherein MRI was done and diagnosed the left knee lateral condyle depressed fracture.
She has undergone surgery on 21.11.2023 for fixation of fracture of fracture site under SA and she was discharged on 22.11.2023 with an advise to take regular follow up treatment.
P.W.1 has further deposed that, she was again admitted to the above said hospital on 09.01.2024 as she had pain.
One infected implant was removed from left proximal tibia and she was SCCH - 26 17 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 discharged on the same day.
P.W.1 has further deposed that, after discharge from the hospital, she took follow up treatment.

Further stated that, due to grievous injuries sustained by her, she cannot do her day to day activities, she cannot walk, sit, squat on the ground, use Indian type toilet, hence she sustained loss of income due to the said accident.

P.W.1 has deposed that, she is not able to do any work and she is permanently disabled.
21.
On the other hand, the advocate for the petitioner vehemently argued that the evidence of PW-2 speaks that the petitioner is suffering from physical permanent disability of 13% to the whole body.
The petitioner became a disabled and unable to do her work as she was working prior to the accident and sustained loss of her future earnings.
In the absence of material documents it is difficult to prove that she was working as nurse prior to the accident.
Therefore the petitioner do not produced any evidence to show that due to the injuries sustained in the accident, she is sustained loss of her future earnings.
The Petitioner has stated that she was aged about 24 years.
As per Ex.P-10, she was aged about 24 years as on alleged accident.

Therefore, she comes under the age group of 20 to 25, the proper multiplier applicable to be the case on hand is '18'.
23.

As per Ex.P.5, Wound Certificate, this Tribunal has come to the conclusion that, in the said road traffic accident, the Petitioner had sustained injuries and it shows that, she has sustained blunt injury to the left knee with (a) fracture of left tibial plateau (b) lateral condyle depressed (c) avulsin of lateral miniscus of left knee and the said injuries are grievous in nature.
The petitioner has taken treatment on 17.11.2023.
Ex .P.11, the discharge summary shows that, the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at Manipal Hospitals from 20.11.2023 to 22.11.2023.
Further she has also taken treatment on 09.11.2023.

sentences.text: Petitioner has also examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N. as P.W.2 and got marked 2 documents as Ex.P.30 and Ex.P.31.

P.W.2 has filed affidavit evidence in lieu of SCCH - 26 19 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 examination in chief and he has stated that, on 06.06.2025, petitioner has contacted him for the assessment of disability.
Further he has deposed that, petitioner has sustained left tibia plateau lateral condyle depression + lateral meniscus avulsion and she has taken treatment at Manipal Hospital.

P.W.2 has deposed that, on examination, the petitioner has wasting of left thigh muscle and restricted left knee movements with severe wasting of the left thigh muscle, X-ray of left knee shows united fracture.
P.W.2 has deposed that, the petitioner has sustained total physical disability of left lower limb at 40% and to the whole body at 13%.
He was cross examined from the side of respondent No.2 at length.
During the course of cross-examination, P.W.2 has deposed that, he was not the treated doctor to the petitioner.
Further admitted that, the injuries are completely cured.
25. By careful perusal of the entire cross-examination of P.W.2, it can be inferred that, he is not the treated doctor.
As such, this Tribunal is declined to consider the entire evidence of P.W.2.

It is well settled law that it is the impact SCCH - 26 20 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

But in the present case, though the petitioner has got examined the doctor as PW.2 to show her disability, but the documents placed on record shows that she has the physical disability at 13% to the whole body.
But by looking into the record it seems that PW.2 has assessed disability of the Petitioner at higher side.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 10% disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.
26. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned, considering the fact that the Petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and in total she was inpatient for a period of 5 days on three occasions, which caused her to immeasurable mental agony and pain.
Hence, I am of the opinion that an amount of Rs.60,000/- would be just and proper compensation under the head pain and sufferings.
SCCH - 26 21 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 27. LOSS OF AMENITIES:-
Further on perusal of evidence of PW.1, it reveals that, petitioner has sustained injuries and the same is mentioned above paras.
The petitioner was aged about 24 years at the time of accident.

Considering the above facts and on perusal of evidence of PW.1 and PW.2 and also considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of loss of amenities.
28. ATTENDANT, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
As per medical bills produced at Ex.P.12, the petitioner took treatment at Manipal Hospital on 17.11.2023 and on 09.01.2024.
The discharge summary produced at Ex.P.11 shows that, the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital for 3 days i.e., from 20.11.2023 to 22.11.2023.
Further, as per Ex.P.22 to Ex.P.27 she took follow-up treatment on several occasions.
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of Rs.7,500/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.

sentences.text: LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As on the date of accident he was aged about 24 years.
Therefore, the appropriate multiplier for the said age group as per Sarla Verma's case is '18'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- p.m.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.3,45,600/- (Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 18 X 10/100) towards loss of future income on the account of disability of the petitioner.
30. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD AND REST PERIOD:-
With regard to loss of earnings during treatment, P.W.1 has deposed that, she could not attend her work for a period of 5 months due to injuries sustained in the accident.
In this regard, P.W.1 has not produced any leave certificate.

By considering 3 days as inpatient and follow up treatment taken by the petitioner on several occasions, around 02 months for rest is considered and loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for two months.

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as Rs.16,000/- per month, Petitioner is awarded SCCH - 26 23 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 Rs.32,000/-
towards loss of earning during laid up period.
31. MEDICAL EXPENSES:-

Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment,
Hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has relied on Ex.P.12 medical bills for Rs.1,44,142/-.
The respondents have disputed the said bills.
On careful perusal of medical bills at Ex.P.12 reveals that, the petitioner has paid certain amount after taking policy discount.
As per Sr.No.16 at Ex.P.12 it reveals that, the petitioner has produced implant removal estimation bill amounting to Rs.1,17,900/-, but she has not produced final bill.
As per the medical bills produced by the petitioner, she has taken policy discount.
Therefore, the Petitioner is not entitled for the amount covered under the bill at Sl.No.16 at Ex.P-12.
After deducting the said amount, the petitioner is entitled to medical expenses of Rs.25,286/- towards Medical Expenses.
32. Future medical expenses:- The petitioner as well as the medical witness have not stated anything about the SCCH - 26 24 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 future medical expenses.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled any compensation towards future medical expenses.

33. By considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion is that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs./- under the following heads:

By considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reasons, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,10,386/-.
Regarding Interest & Liability:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
35. The Respondent No.1 is the RC owner of offending KTM Avenger-250 Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KL- 8554 and Respondent No.2 is the insurer.
Hence, both the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to the compensation to the Petitioner.

However, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending KTM Avenger-250 Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KL-855 is liable to pay compensation Rs.5,10,386/- with 6% interest to the petitioner from the date of petition till deposit the amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the 'Partly affirmative'.

36. Issue No.3: in view of my finding on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,10,386/- (Rupees Five lakhs ten thousand three hundred and eighty six Only) with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However, the respondent No.2 being insurer of offending motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 04-JM-8554 is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.

 :: Judgment:
opennyai_summary.facts:
:
The petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking to award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in the road traffic accident.
She was maintained her family members, since she is the only earning member in the family.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the KTM Avenger-250 Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KL-8554 by its rider and in this connection, the Hebbal Traffic Police have registered the case in Cr.No.214/2023 and filed charge sheet punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC against the said rider.
At the time of accident, the first respondent being the R.C owner of the aforesaid KTM Avenger-250 motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 04-KL-8554 and the 2nd respondent being the insurer, the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
7. Respondent No.1-R.C. owner of the offending vehicle has filed objection by denying the entire petition averments.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is contended that, the petitioner had to wait for the bus at the bus shelter on the footpath provided for the safety of the commuters, but she had stepped down on the road and thereby she has violated the traffic rules, hence the accident SCCH - 26 8 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 was occurred due to own negligence of the petitioner.
Without proper investigation the police have registered the case against the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04- KL-8554 to help the petitioner only to get compensation.
The owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
The rider of offending vehicle had no valid driving licence to ride the same as on the date of accident, which is clear violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence this respondent is not liable to pay compensation.
opennyai_summary.issue:
9. On the basis of the above pleadings, following issues have been framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, on 17.11.2023 at about 6.50 a.m., when she was standing on the extreme left side at Devinagara Cross Bus stop, Bhadrappa layout,
Bangalore, at that time, the rider of the KRM Avenger-25- Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KL-8554 came from Hebbal towards B.E.L. SCCH - 26 9 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 side in a rash and negligent manner without observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident, due to the impact, she was fell down sustained grievous injuries mentioned in the petition?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?
If so,
from which respondent?
3. What Order or Award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Per-contra, the respondent No.1 and 2 have denied the income of petitioner.
In order to prove her avocation and income, the petitioner has not examined her employer.
But she has not produced any bank statement to show that, she was drawing salary of Rs.28,000/- per month.
Therefore the petitioner has failed to prove that, she was drawing salary of Rs.28,000/- per month at the time of accident.
Hence this Tribunal is unable to considered the income of the petitioner as Rs.28,000/- per month at the time of accident.
At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision of Yashoda.H and others V/s. Sharath Kumar Achar and another.
In this case, the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore, in view of the above decision,
Gangamma C vs Deekshith M on 12 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57391937/
6
the accident was occurred during the year 2023.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.
Further admitted that, the injuries are completely cured.
25. By careful perusal of the entire cross-examination of P.W.2, it can be inferred that, he is not the treated doctor.
As such, this Tribunal is declined to consider the entire evidence of P.W.2.
It is well settled law that it is the impact SCCH - 26 20 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
But in the present case, though the petitioner has got examined the doctor as PW.2 to show her disability, but the documents placed on record shows that she has the physical disability at 13% to the whole body.
But by looking into the record it seems that PW.2 has assessed disability of the Petitioner at higher side.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 10% disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.3,45,600/- (Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 18 X 10/100) towards loss of future income on the account of disability of the petitioner.

 Sl. Compensation heads Compensati  No. on amount  1. Loss of future earning Rs. 3,45,600/-

TOTAL Rs.5,10,386/-
By considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reasons, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,10,386/-.
Hence, both the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to the compensation to the Petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending KTM Avenger-250 Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KL-855 is liable to pay compensation Rs.5,10,386/- with 6% interest to the petitioner from the date of petition till deposit the amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the 'Partly affirmative'.
36. Issue No.3: in view of my finding on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
SCCH - 26 26 M.V.C.No.7730/2023
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,10,386/- (Rupees Five lakhs ten thousand three hundred and eighty six Only) with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, the respondent No.2 being insurer of offending motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 04-JM-8554 is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
After deposit the award amount, entire amount with accrued interest shall be released in favour of petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
